sections.summary: This summary provides key information about the EuroStable asset-referenced token (ART). It is intended to support the prospective holder in making an informed decision. The summary covers the issuer and its authorisation, the referenced assets and the mechanism that aligns the value of the reserve with the claim, the rights of holders including the permanent right of redemption at the market value of the referenced assets, the principal risks, the reserve composition and segregation, the technology, and the redemption procedure. The full white paper, including the management body statement, must be read alongside this summary and is the controlling document for the offer.
sections.risk_warning: The crypto-asset described in this white paper may lose its value in part or in full, may not always be transferable, and may not be liquid. Past performance of the EuroStable ART is not indicative of future performance. The crypto-asset is not covered by an investor compensation scheme or a deposit guarantee scheme. The risk of total loss is real and the holder should not invest amounts that cannot be lost in full.
sections.management_statement: The management body of the issuer declares that this white paper complies with the requirements of Regulation (EU) 2023/1114 (MiCAR), that the information presented is fair, clear, and not misleading, and that no information has been omitted that would be material to the assessment of the asset-referenced token. The management body assumes responsibility for the content of this white paper.
sections.notification_date: Date of notification to the competent authority: 2 March 2026 (synthetic fixture date for the reviewer demo).
sections.language: This white paper is drawn up in English, a language customary in the sphere of international finance, and a German-language translation is available upon request from the issuer.
sections.issuer: EuroStable AG is a fictional synthetic issuer used only for this local fixture. The legal form used in the fixture is a stock corporation (Aktiengesellschaft) organised under the laws of the Federal Republic of Germany, with a fictional registered seat and business address at Example Street 80, 10115 Berlin, and a fictional register reference HRB 000000. No real BaFin authorisation is asserted; the fixture assumes an ART authorisation field remains under lawyer review. The management body consists of three fictional members with combined prior experience in regulated payment services, treasury management, and information security. Its fictional Legal Entity Identifier (LEI), synthetic and not registered, is 9999SYNTHEUROSTB0184.
sections.art: The EuroStable ART is an asset-referenced token within the meaning of Art. 3(1)(6) MiCAR. Its characteristics: each token gives its holder a claim on the issuer and, where the issuer cannot meet its obligations, in respect of the reserve of assets, and it references a basket of EUR-denominated short-dated sovereign debt instruments issued by Member States of the euro area and of cash deposits at credit institutions authorised in the European Union. Issuance and redemption at the market value of the referenced assets keep its value stable. The persons involved in its operationalisation are the issuer, a fictional technology provider and the fictional reserve custodian. The plans for the token set out its past and future milestones: a closed pilot with authorised participants ended in March 2026, public issuance starts after notification, and admission to a second trading platform is planned for 2027.
sections.offer_or_admission: This crypto-asset white paper concerns an offer to the public of the EuroStable ART. The prospective holders targeted by the offer are professional clients, eligible counterparties and retail customers in Germany and Austria. Tokens are issued at the reference value plus a fixed subscription fee. Admission to trading on a crypto-asset trading platform may follow at the discretion of the issuer. The law applicable to the offer is German law, and the competent courts are those of Frankfurt am Main.
sections.rights_and_obligations: The holder of the EuroStable ART has the following rights against the issuer: a permanent right of redemption at all times in accordance with Art. 39 MiCAR, paid in euro at the market value of the referenced assets, a right to file complaints under the procedure described in Section 9 of this white paper, and information rights regarding the composition of the reserve. The obligations of the holder include compliance with applicable transfer restrictions, sanctions screening, and the issuer's terms of service. The redemption right may not be waived by contract and is enforceable in the courts of the Federal Republic of Germany. The claim each token represents references two assets in specified proportions: 70% short-dated EUR-denominated sovereign debt instruments issued by Member States of the euro area and 30% cash deposits at credit institutions authorised in the European Union. The claim is valued at the market value of those referenced assets: the issuer's middle office values its components daily from independent market prices, and a fictional independent valuation agent reviews the valuation each month.
sections.technology: The EuroStable ART is issued, transferred and stored on a permissioned distributed ledger operated by a fictional third party on the issuer's behalf. Its protocol uses a Byzantine fault tolerant consensus mechanism, and validators receive a fixed fee instead of transaction-based incentives. Smart contract modules govern issuance, redemption, and supply control. Two independent code security firms audited the technology in February 2026 and April 2026, and the audit outcome left no critical finding open. Custody of the technical keys rests with a regulated custodian using multi-party computation.
sections.risks: The principal risks attached to the EuroStable ART are grouped by source. Reserve of assets: if the issuer cannot meet its obligations, holders depend on the reserve, whose market value may fall below the aggregate claims of the outstanding tokens. Issuer: the issuer may fail operationally or financially, including in insolvency, and a sanctions designation of a reserve counterparty may freeze part of the reserve. Offer: the secondary market price of the token may diverge from the reference value, and liquidity may be thin during a redemption surge. Token and referenced assets: the value of the referenced sovereign debt may fall, and credit risk arises on each reserve counterparty. Operationalisation: delays in onboarding authorised participants may disrupt issuance and redemption. Technology: smart contract failure, key compromise or validator failure may stop transfers; mitigation measures include independent code audits, multi-party computation for keys and a tested incident response plan. Reserve impairment events trigger the cure procedure described in Section 11. Redemption may be suspended only under the recovery plan or by the competent authority under Art. 46 MiCAR, and never to manage commercial outcomes.
sections.reserve_of_assets: The reserve of assets is composed of short-dated EUR-denominated sovereign debt issued by Member States of the euro area with residual maturity of less than ninety days, and of overnight cash deposits at credit institutions authorised in the European Union. This synthetic draft states that 30% of the amount referenced in euro is held as deposits with credit institutions. The composition of the reserve is fixed within a defined target band and rebalanced on a quarterly cycle. The mechanism aimed at aligning the value of the reserve with the claim of the outstanding tokens is a daily reconciliation, and any shortfall is restored within one business day. The reserve is held by a separate special-purpose vehicle and is segregated from the issuer's own balance sheet by way of a security trust structure. Custody is provided by a fictional Tier-1 European credit institution acting as qualified custodian under a tri-party custody and segregation agreement. The valuation of the reserve is performed daily at fair value by the issuer's middle office and verified weekly by the custodian. The reserve is audited monthly by an independent statutory auditor and reconciled against the outstanding token supply on a continuous basis through automated supply oracles. Any shortfall triggers the cure procedure described in Section 11 and would be routed to lawyer review for any required authority notification.
sections.environmental_impact: The consensus mechanism used by the issuance protocol is a permissioned Byzantine fault tolerant variant that does not rely on proof-of-work and does not consume energy at the level of public proof-of-work chains. The issuer monitors the energy consumption of the validator infrastructure on a continuous basis and publishes annual environmental and climate-related impact data in line with the ESMA regulatory technical standards on sustainability indicators for distributed ledger technology. Validators source electricity from the European mainland grid, with a contracted renewable share that is reported alongside the annual disclosure. The methodology, scope, and limitations of the climate-related disclosures are described in Annex 2.
sections.redemption: The holder may exercise the permanent right of redemption against the issuer at all times. The issuer redeems by paying euro, other than electronic money, equal to the market value of the referenced assets when the request is processed. The procedure requires a KYC-verified redemption request submitted through the issuer's portal. The timeframe for settlement is one business day from receipt of a complete redemption request, with cut-off at 16:00 CET for same-cycle processing. Redemption is settled by EUR bank transfer to the holder's verified bank account. Redemption is not subject to a fee (Art. 39(3) MiCAR). Only the recovery plan under Art. 46 MiCAR may provide for liquidity fees, limits on daily redemptions or a suspension of redemptions, and the competent authority may temporarily suspend redemption under Art. 46(4) MiCAR; any suspension is published on the issuer's portal.
